title: Lightweight Machine-Learning Models for ECG Classification

pico.comparator: no intervention, usual care or any control
pico.setting: resource-constrained devices: microcontroller, wearable, smartphone, FPGA

inclusion_criteria: Machine-learning model that classifies ECG signals or heartbeats
The model separates abnormal from normal ECG (binary output, or abnormal classes reported against normal)
Model evaluated for or on a resource-constrained device (microcontroller, wearable, smartphone or FPGA)
At least one efficiency metric reported (model size, memory, latency, power or energy)
full_text_criteria: At least one efficiency metric reported (model size, memory, latency, power or energy)
design_reason: Best design to evaluate the effectiveness of machine-learning models.

criterion_labels.criterion: Machine-learning model that classifies ECG signals or heartbeats
criterion_labels.label: not an ECG classifier

criterion_labels.criterion: The model separates abnormal from normal ECG (binary output, or abnormal classes reported against normal)
criterion_labels.label: no abnormal vs normal task

criterion_labels.criterion: Model evaluated for or on a resource-constrained device (microcontroller, wearable, smartphone or FPGA)
criterion_labels.label: no constrained device

criterion_labels.criterion: At least one efficiency metric reported (model size, memory, latency, power or energy)
criterion_labels.label: no efficiency metric

criterion_evidence.criterion: Model evaluated for or on a resource-constrained device (microcontroller, wearable, smartphone or FPGA)
At least one efficiency metric reported (model size, memory, latency, power or energy)

rationale: The research question focuses on the effectiveness of lightweight machine-learning models in detecting abnormal ECG signals on resource-constrained devices. The PICO framework helps to clearly define the population, intervention, comparator, outcomes, and setting.
question: Which lightweight machine-learning models detect abnormal versus normal ECG on resource-constrained devices (microcontroller, wearable, smartphone, FPGA), and how accurate and efficient are they?
database_reason: Relevant for health and machine learning research.
criteria_source: topics.yaml T2 (review none (new review; no published systematic review asks this, searched 2026-11-08))

extraction_fields.dataset: ECG database(s) used (e.g. MIT-BIH, PTB-XL, INCART) and number of records or subjects
extraction_fields.classes: Classes the model outputs and their number (e.g. AAMI N, S, V, F, Q; normal vs abnormal)
extraction_fields.partition: Evaluation protocol as stated: how data were split between training and test (inter-patient, intra-patient / random beats, patient-specific)
extraction_fields.model: Model family and topology (e.g. 1D-CNN, LSTM, SVM, spiking network, transformer)
extraction_fields.operations: Operation count per classification (MACs, OPs or FLOPs, as printed)
extraction_fields.parameters: Parameter count of the deployed model
extraction_fields.arithmetic: Arithmetic width of the deployed model (e.g. float32, int8, binary, fixed point)
extraction_fields.memory: Memory footprint of the deployed model (kB), and peak activation memory if given
extraction_fields.platform: Target hardware platform and technology (microcontroller, FPGA, ASIC node, SoC, smartphone), as named
extraction_fields.latency: Inference latency or time per classification on the target
extraction_fields.power_energy: Power consumption and/or energy per classification on the target
extraction_fields.classification_metrics: All classification metrics reported (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, F1, per class if given), and whether they are for the deployed variant or the software model

checklist_domains.name: Evaluation protocol stated
checklist_domains.question: Is the evaluation protocol (how ECG records or subjects were divided between training and test) explicitly stated?

checklist_domains.name: Subjects separated between training and test
checklist_domains.question: Does the protocol separate subjects between training and test? Low for an inter-patient partition, unclear for a patient-specific one, high otherwise (e.g. intra-patient or random beat split).

checklist_domains.name: Per-class or prevalence-insensitive metric
checklist_domains.question: Is a per-class or prevalence-insensitive metric reported (e.g. per-class sensitivity and PPV, macro-F1), not only overall accuracy?

checklist_domains.name: Deployed variant evaluated
checklist_domains.question: Can the classification quality of the variant actually deployed on the device be separated from the best software result?

checklist_domains.name: Model size reported
checklist_domains.question: Is a parameter count or a memory footprint of the model reported?
